title: Decompose large control-plane JSONB blobs into normalized columns and introduce hot-index tiers
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Background: Our control-plane stores several tenant and project metadata blobs as a single JSONB column (metadata_blob) on the projects and tenant_entities tables. Over time these blobs have grown and are queried for a handful of high-cardinality fields (owner_id, plan_tier, external_id, last_sync_ts), while the rest of the JSON is rarely read. The current pattern results in wide rows, slow index usage, frequent full-row fetches and expensive sequential scans in queries used by the console and API hot paths.

Goal: Reduce control-plane query latency and downstream CPU by decomposing frequently-read JSONB keys into first-class columns with targeted indexes, while keeping a compact "shadow" JSONB for rare or write-heavy keys. Introduce a two-tier index strategy: hot-indexes (covering the common query sets with covering indexes) and cold-indexes (sparser indexes for analytical queries). Ensure online migrations, safe rollouts and small-window backfills so production latency is not disrupted.

Scope: projects.metadata_blob and tenant_entities.meta_blob. This ticket covers schema changes, online migration runner, backfill orchestration, new covering indexes, query rewrite guidance, runtime feature-flagging and dashboards for monitoring regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Add typed columns for owner_id, plan_tier, external_id, last_sync_ts on both projects and tenant_entities without table rewrite at creation (use ADD COLUMN with default NULL).

Create hot covering indexes that satisfy the top-10 control-plane hot queries (verified by EXPLAIN plans on prod-like dataset) and reduce 95th percentile latency of those queries by >=40% in staging tests.
Provide an online backfill job that streams rows in bounded transactions, tracks progress, supports resume, and can be rate-limited to avoid replication lag spikes.
Introduce a migration toggle (DB feature flag) to switch reads to new columns; ability to fall back to JSONB read if column is NULL.
Run backfill to 95%+ completion for a single tenant in staging and validate no tail latency regressions during backfill window.
Add observability: per-query latency dashboards, rows-remaining backfill gauge, index size and bloat metrics; create an alert if replication lag > 30s during migration.
Document query rewrites and add a small set of ORM helpers in repo to prefer columns but fall back to JSON extraction for legacy rows.
Ship migration scripts and a PR with tests; get sign-off from Database Reliability and Platform Security teams.
tasks: Draft schema DDL and review with DB reliability (Marcus + SRE)

Implement online backfill runner (worker) with resume and rate-limit hooks
Add ORM helpers and update 4 hottest query callsites to prefer new columns
Create migration runbook and rollout plan including canary tenant list
Add Prometheus exporters for backfill progress and index size; wire to Grafana
Open PR for DDL + worker + app changes; include migration tests and benchmark scripts
Perform staged rollout: staging full backfill -> canary tenant -> gradual ramp across tenants

notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping the JSONB allows write schema flexibility but hurts read performance; upfront cost is backfill IO and index bloat vs long-term query savings.
Rollback plan: remove read path preference and rely on JSONB; optionally drop columns (no inline) if rollback required after all tenants are on JSON-free reads.
Edge cases: historical rows with malformed JSON will be skipped and recorded in a remediation queue for manual reconciliation. Worker emits a remediation record per row with failure reason.

Performance knobs: backfill concurrency, batch size, and index creation schedule (create indexes after bulk fills vs before to reduce writes). We chose to create indexes before backfill to gain fast query wins for migrated rows and to keep backfill idempotent.
